Bug_Details: Period.get() only works with YEARS, MONTHS, or DAYS. Period.get(TemporalUnit) only works when passed ChronoUnit.YEARS, ChronoUnit.MONTHS, or ChronoUnit.DAYS. All other values are guaranteed to throw an UnsupportedTemporalTypeException.
Bug_Explanation: The bug is that Period.get() is called with ChronoUnit.SECONDS, which is not supported and causes an UnsupportedTemporalTypeException to be thrown.
Trigger_Explanation: The test case calls the showBug() method from the PeriodBugExample class, which internally calls period.get(ChronoUnit.SECONDS). This triggers an UnsupportedTemporalTypeException because ChronoUnit.SECONDS is not a supported unit for the Period.get() method.
